rows.grounds: abstract noun from nirarthaka (without-purpose); nominative subject of implied result
genitive dependent indicating whose meaninglessness is asserted
locative indicating the domain or activity in which meaninglessness would arise
consequential particle/pronoun drawing the inference from the preceding denial of bondage and liberation
locative indicating ascertainment or establishing of that matter as another affected domain

items.question: What consequence follows for scripture if bondage and liberation are denied?
premises: The preceding verses deny the reality of bondage and liberation because all states are Śiva.
Scripture functions in enjoining action and in determining matters such as bondage and liberation.
If its objects or determinations lack reality, scripture loses its operative purpose.
items.inference: Therefore, denying bondage and liberation entails the meaninglessness of scripture in both enjoining action and determining that state.
uncertainties: Whether karaṇe refers specifically to ritual action or more broadly to any prescriptive activity.
Whether nirūpaṇe refers to determining bondage and liberation or to doctrinal determination in general.
items.plain_english: Then scripture would be meaningless, both in prescribing action and in determining that matter.
